item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"medium","summary":"B is preferable because it explicitly implements the required Upload validation, preserves Add’s option-processing order, and provides clearer multipart and retry verification. Both patches still require contract-alignment changes before merge.","reasons":["B explicitly rejects an empty filename and nil content before constructing the multipart body; A delegates this implicitly to multipartbody.NewFile.","B preserves Add’s existing newFilesOptions call order, while A moves option processing until after the entire body has been read.","B separately verifies multipart field/name/content and retrying streamed content from an os.File, making failures easier to diagnose.","Both propagate multipartbody.NewFile errors and reuse the established helper."],"risks_a":["Upload calls the new private add method instead of FilesService.Add, contrary to the required routing.","Add is changed to unconditionally buffer caller-supplied bodies, altering its existing streaming behavior and memory profile.","No visible tests cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader errors."],"risks_b":["Upload also bypasses FilesService.Add through a new private add method.","Add is unnecessarily changed to buffer all custom multipart bodies, violating the instruction to preserve its behavior.","The required validation and source-reader error cases are not covered by visible tests; validation also combines two distinct failures into one generic error."]}
